name: OpenBSD
summary: A security-oriented Unix system whose monolithic kernel combines process and thread management with explicit syscall and filesystem restriction primitives and stateful packet filtering.

features.name: Process and thread kernel boundary
features.description: OpenBSD maintains distinct process and thread structures, allocates them through kernel pools, and creates new processes or threads through fork-family paths.
benefits: Provides a Unix process API while supporting kernel-managed threads and explicit parent-child lifecycle state.
costs: The monolithic kernel shares privileged address space and subsystem state, so process isolation does not remove kernel-wide fault impact.

features.name: Irreversible pledge capability reduction
features.description: pledge divides system operations into named promise groups; a process may reduce its available groups, and disallowed operations are blocked or terminate the process according to the documented mode.
benefits: Makes intended syscall capability reduction explicit and composable with process lifecycle.
costs: Programs must know their future operation set, and irreversible reduction can expose integration failures when assumptions are incomplete.

features.name: Unveil path and filesystem visibility
features.description: unveil records per-process path permissions and can lock further changes, restricting filesystem operations to declared paths and permissions.
benefits: Adds a path-oriented boundary complementary to operation-level pledge restrictions.
costs: Path rules, directory matching, and post-exec behavior require careful configuration; the mechanism is advisory to application design rather than automatic policy synthesis.

features.name: Stateful packet-filtering subsystem
features.description: The fixed source contains PF rule, state, queue, and address-pool structures and routines that evaluate packets and maintain stateful filtering data.
benefits: Provides an in-kernel policy and state boundary for network traffic.
costs: Rule evaluation, state tracking, and kernel integration create substantial policy and concurrency complexity.

mathematical_views.question: How do OpenBSD process records, thread records, parent links, and credentials compose during fork and thread creation?
assumptions: Processes and threads are distinct typed nodes.
The view abstracts architecture-specific context setup and scheduler details.

mathematical_views.question: How do pledge promise reductions and unveil path permissions constrain a process over time?
assumptions: Policies only lose permissions after establishment.
Operation and path policies are modeled as intersecting capability sets, not as complete security proofs.

mathematical_views.question: How do PF rules and state records determine packet treatment over a flow lifetime?
assumptions: Flows have state records and packet observations.
The view abstracts device and protocol-specific details and does not claim policy correctness.
